I wrote the screening result to `/home/mara/cwe-bench/sibling2/out/screener/27788.json`.

- **Trust decision:** `FileServer` lets a user read a file only if they can access the component named in the `ComponentId` parameter. A missing `ComponentId` counted as "Personal space" and was always allowed, and a `TypeUpload` parameter turned `SourceFile`/`Directory` into absolute filesystem paths (`core-war/src/main/java/org/silverpeas/web/servlets/FileServer.java:150-152`, `:120-121`).
- **`pattern_fit`:** B. The real fix is all in one servlet; the `FileServerUtils` changes only remove unused code.
- **Strongest lever:** two routes into the same file sink still skip the access check after the fix. The mail-time HTML scanner (`FileServer.java:179-191`) can be dismissed as "server-side mail rendering". `OnlineFileServer.java:58-99` has no session or component check at all, and can be dismissed as "the public online file server".
- **Biggest red flag:** none of the listed flags apply. The risks are that `OnlineFileServer` may be public on purpose, which would weaken that route, and that there are no tests for these servlets. Behavioural tests would need a mocked servlet and session harness. I didn't measure the build or the repo size.
